title: SPIN Aims to Reclaim Its Place in the Meetings Industry
summary: SPIN spent years as a members-only Facebook group. Now it wants a seat alongside MPI and PCMA. Can a free, volunteer-run association of veteran planners build that kind of influence?

title: Is It Time to Say "Last Call" to the Open Bar?
summary: The open bar is no longer the default icebreaker. Planners who pair quality zero-proof drinks with activities and smarter timing give every attendee a reason to stay and connect. At Skift Meetings Forum 2026, planners compared notes on shrinking bar tabs, pricey mocktails, and receptions built around more than drinks.

title: Cybercriminals Invented an Entire Conference — and Used a Real Hotel to Sell the Lie
summary: With prominent scientists, corporate sponsors, and a Boston hotel venue, the conference website looked legitimate. The scam is a reminder that the professional credibility of speaking at a meeting can be weaponized by criminals.

title: Bigger Meeting Budgets, Tighter Scrutiny: What Planners Expect in 2027
summary: Meeting budgets are growing, but rising costs and geopolitical uncertainty are forcing planners to rethink how they spend. Amex GBT’s latest forecast reveals another vulnerability: Organizations are managing risk without consistently incorporating safety and security into formal meeting policies.

title: 5 LEED-Certified Convention Centers You Should Know About
summary: It’s not just features that add up to LEED certification. These convention centers are known for working closely with event customers to share their meetings’ sustainability stories.

title: Grace Hopper Cancels Two Weeks Out, but Its Community Is Gathering Anyway
summary: The conference couldn’t survive a shortfall in registrations and sponsorships. But its community is finding ways to gather without it, raising questions about whether the value of a conference ultimately belongs to its organizer or its attendees.

title: Steal These Ideas: 10 CSR Activities and Gifts From IMEX and Beyond
summary: Giving back has become the norm on the convention floor, and these 10 options were inspired by IMEX America.

title: The AI Paradox Looming Over the Meetings Industry
summary: AI may turn out to be the best demand driver meetings have had in years. But attendees will increasingly discover events through chatbots, plan their schedules with AI, and arrive accustomed to digital interactions. Delivering the human connection they seek could prove harder than the industry assumes.

title: One Woman Leader on the Importance of Curiosity
summary: The new interim CEO of the incentive industry’s major association, SITE, Rebecca Wright will initially focus on questioning, listening, and learning.

title: At IMEX America, Optimism Comes With a Price Tag
summary: IMEX America proved the meetings industry still wants to gather. The question heading into 2027 is how much organizations will pay for the privilege.
